quote: But if the government's gonna pay for it, I will go I'll I'll go for that.
stewart_read: This is a live conditional-interest hook; instead of pivoting to the interest_question/bill anchor, rep corrects the tax-credit fact and lets the thread die.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically holding qualifiers until legitimacy settled, but nothing in the next several turns shows any attempt to return to verify, undermining that read.
coaching_implication: Should have followed the tax-credit correction immediately with the interest_question ('what got you looking at solar in the first place?') to re-anchor before the customer wandered.

quote: I wasn't looking for a tax credit. I was looking for a freebie.
stewart_read: This is a cost-expectation objection in disguise; rep answers literally ('they don't pay for solar') instead of flipping to what the customer's current bill costs him every month.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this too early in the call (before qualification) to use a flip; but the schema explicitly says flips apply in the first 5 minutes, which this is well within.
coaching_implication: Coach the flip: 'It's not free, but what you're paying your utility every month basically is your freebie going to them instead of your roof.'

quote: To be honest, I'm not too sure, like, what the pricing looks like because I'm just a scheduler.
stewart_read: Honest admission of scope limits is fine in spirit, but rep never redirects to the specialist/appointment value using the escape hatch language; it lands as a dead end instead of a bridge.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive gap, not strategic — no follow-up sentence attempts to convert the admission into a booking pitch.
coaching_implication: Pair the scope-limit admission with the universal escape hatch: 'That's exactly what our specialist can walk you through with real numbers for your home.'

quote: Yeah. Yeah. That's funny. That's what happens when you leave your phone number.

alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as adequate light rapport since customer laughs it off, but the same anxiety resurfaces at 03:15 as the reason for exit, showing it wasn't defused.
coaching_implication: Use protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number style specificity here — reference the form/request directly to differentiate Ion from spam callers.

coaching_implication: After acknowledging, bridge back to the appointment: use the moment to reassure legitimacy and re-anchor to the customer's original interest.

quote: alright. Well, anyway, the answer is no. I'm not interested.

coaching_implication: At minimum acknowledge-then-small-ask, or use changed_mind curiosity language ('did you get a chance to see actual numbers for your home?') before letting him go.
